authoredFrom: Erlang semantics + the pinned grammar's generator shape, before this fixture's F3 run. Four pattern-position classes, each of which decided a different defect the corpus dual lens found: a `when` GUARD computes (`X#r.f > 0` is a member READ); a comprehension GENERATOR's left side binds whatever expression holds the comprehension (`[N || #r{f = N} <- L]` is a match, and the `<-` sits inside a `generator` node — both the analyzer and the independent oracle first missed that and agreed on the wrong answer, which is the case a mirror cannot see); a case arm's `Y = #r{}` is a pattern even though the record is on the match's VALUE side; and a body match `A = #r{}` IS a construction. Complexity is 1 + arms: gen and comp carry one comprehension each, arm carries two cr_clauses. Lines are read off the fixture text.
